method: WebSearch/WebFetch only; ~8 searches, ~17 fetches. Several primary pages (quantinuum.com blog/press, whitehouse.gov, hpcwire, phys.org) could not be fetched, so details come from secondary write-ups and are flagged.

developments.what: Helios trapped-ion machine, color-code logical memory at distances 3/5/7 (up to 37 physical qubits per logical qubit): 99.9995% logical fidelity (~5 errors per million), ~10x better than the company's September Helix-code result; reported error suppression factor ~12 per distance step (logical gates ~9).
developments.why_it_matters: Clear below-threshold scaling with distance on commercial hardware; supports the Apollo 2029 fault-tolerance target. Caveats: vendor-reported, not peer reviewed; memory-style metric, not a full universal computation; the 'teraquop' extrapolation (distance ~21) is a projection; post-selection status not confirmed in sources I could read.

developments.who: Google Quantum AI (Gidney, Shutty, Jones et al.)
developments.what: Science paper: experimental magic state cultivation on Willow, ~40x error reduction vs uncultivated states, T-state fidelity >= 0.9999, ~8% of attempts retained (post-selected), grafted from distance-3 color code into distance-5 surface code.
developments.why_it_matters: First hardware demonstration of the cheap magic-state method that cuts a major fault-tolerance overhead (earlier estimates: up to ~95% of machine capacity). Post-selection with 8% yield and small scale limit immediate practicality; the 40x is relative to uncultivated states, not other distillation methods.

developments.what: Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ advance to QBI Stage C (joining Microsoft and PsiQuantum from US2QC). Quantinuum, QuEra, Xanadu, Nord Quantique, Photonic, Quantum Motion and SQC remain in Stage B, not eliminated.
developments.why_it_matters: Independent government vetting of utility-scale plans; Stage C is 'plans to proof'. Notable that Quantinuum and QuEra were not in this cohort. Read as a screening milestone, not a performance result.

developments.who: Quantinuum with JPMorgan Chase et al. (Perlin et al.), published in a APS journal
developments.what: End-to-end fault-tolerant QAOA and HHL runs on H2/Helios with the [[7,1,3]] Steane code; largest QAOA used 12 logical qubits (97 physical, 2,132 two-qubit gates); logical T gate infidelity reported ~2.6e-3.
developments.why_it_matters: Among the largest logical-level algorithm executions to date, but performance only 'better than random', uses post-selection/repeat-until-success, and the sources I read have inconsistent T-gate figures; check paper before citing numbers.

developments.what: Silicon spin qubits: single-qubit gate fidelity >99.99% with three qubits driven in parallel on a five-qubit array sharing one microwave line (others ~99.9%).
developments.why_it_matters: Reduces a known crosstalk/scaling risk for spin qubits; academic, incremental, single-qubit gates only.
developments.date_note: Reported Oct 2026; exact date approximate (covered Oct 17-19).

developments.what: Decoder and QEC-tooling results: GPU-accelerated decoder calibration (~65x), parallel GPU decoding of LDPC-cat codes via NVQLink, AI-agent-designed decoder hardware for the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle code (52x faster HLS estimates).
developments.why_it_matters: Real-time decoding is a practical bottleneck for QEC; incremental engineering, mostly vendor claims.

developments.what: Compact codes encoding more than one logical qubit per two physical data qubits on reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays, distance 12 (principles published Sept 2026 per the digest).
developments.why_it_matters: High-rate codes cut overhead if realized; date and experimental vs theoretical status unclear from the secondary source, needs verification.

not_found: No new quantum-advantage claim by a major lab and no classical rebuttal dated within Oct 1-24 found. The Flatiron tensor-network rebuttal of D-Wave and D-Wave's response are from ~May 2026, outside the window.
No major vendor roadmap change found in window (IBM Starling/Quantinuum Apollo 2029 targets unchanged; QuEra 1,000 logical qubits by 2029 and IonQ 2M qubits by 2030 are restatements/targets).

Policy: reported US administration 2028 quantum-for-science target (October fact sheet) and DOE eight priority applications; could not fetch the primary source, so not rated as a technical development.

overhyped.claim: Quantinuum '99.9995%' and 'approaching one million error-free operations'
overhyped.reason: Logical memory fidelity per round under vendor measurement, not a million-gate computation; extrapolations (teraquop at distance ~21, 30x fewer qubits) are projections; not peer reviewed or independently reproduced. The real news is the clean ~12x per-distance suppression.

overhyped.claim: ORCA PT-3 'first quantum computer built for commercial quantum advantage' and its 12x speedup over its predecessor
overhyped.reason: Speedup is relative to ORCA's own previous system, not the best classical solver; no classical baseline shown; marketing framing.

overhyped.claim: Google magic state cultivation '40x error reduction'
overhyped.reason: Measured against uncultivated states, with ~8% post-selection yield and small-scale demo; a real milestone but not a 40x improvement over existing distillation.

overhyped.claim: 'Is Quantinuum now ahead of Google?' / vendor-hosted 'independent study' showing Quantinuum outperforming superconducting systems
overhyped.reason: Comparisons are across different codes, distances and metrics, and the study was hosted on Quantinuum's own blog (could not verify authorship); Lambda 12 vs 1.56 compares different architectures.

overhyped.claim: LLM-designed circuits (Anthropic/Harvard/QuEra) cutting FeMoco gate count to ~340M
overhyped.reason: Resource-estimate improvement on paper, not a hardware result; counts are still far beyond current devices.

overhyped.claim: IonQ '2 million qubits by 2030' and QuEra '1,000 logical qubits by 2029'
overhyped.reason: Roadmap targets coupled to financing announcements, not demonstrated capability.
